s1.text: Rain taps the window. On the desk, a notebook lies open to a page that ends mid-sentence.

s2.speaker: @companion
s2.text: Ah — don't read that yet! It's… not finished. It hasn't been finished for three weeks.

s3.speaker: @companion
s3.text: It's a letter to my younger self. I keep stopping at the same line: "Someday, you will…"

choices.text: "Maybe it doesn't need an ending yet."

s4a.speaker: @companion
s4a.text: Because whatever I write becomes a promise. And what if I can't keep it?

s4b.speaker: @companion
s4b.text: …Huh. I never thought an empty line could be allowed to just exist.

s5.text: She turns the pencil over in her fingers. The lamp hums. Somewhere a kettle clicks off.

s6.speaker: @companion
s6.text: Will you sit with me while I try? Just for one focus session.

choices.text: "Of course. I'll work on my own page too."
"You've got this. I'll check in after."

s7.text: You both write in silence. Pages fill. The rain softens into a whisper.

s7b.text: You step away. Through the doorway you hear the pencil — hesitant, then steady.

s8.speaker: @companion
s8.text: "Someday, you will…" {flag:gentle|— no. I'll leave it open. That's the point, isn't it?|— finish what you start, one small page at a time.}

s9.speaker: @companion
s9.text: {flag:stayed|Thank you for staying. It was easier with company.|Thanks for believing I could.} …Same time tomorrow?

end.text: — End of Chapter 1: The Unfinished Page —
